_doc: Operational sources. This is the ONE place for arXiv categories and YouTube search queries (scripts/fetch_candidates.py reads them). config/interests.json says what you care about; this file says where to look.

arxiv._doc: Categories chosen for coverage, not completeness. Volume-heavy categories get higher limits so a 4-day lookback (covers weekends) isn't truncated. arXiv allows one request every 3 seconds on one connection; the fetcher spaces calls, retries 429/5xx with backoff, and falls back to rss.arxiv.org per category.

coverage._doc: Every topic in config/interests.json -> established.ai_research has an entry here: where its papers appear (categories) and phrases that identify it (keywords). A keyword counts only when the paper is in one of the topic's categories (or has no categories, as with trending papers). Keywords of up to 4 characters match whole words (llm, rag); longer ones match word starts (agentic matches agentic, retriev matches retrieval). Keep keywords specific: generic words such as 'evaluation' or 'stability' match half of arXiv. weight scales relevance (0.5 broad, 2 boosted). Used by dsys/rank.py and checked by validation.

ranking._doc: Pre-ranking in code, before Claude reads any abstract (dsys/rank.py). Relevance comes from the coverage keywords, quality signals add to it. The shortlist takes the best per_interest papers for every interest first, then fills up to shortlist_size by score. Claude reads those abstracts plus every trending or notable paper.

research_updates.note: X/Twitter and LinkedIn posts are only included when reachable and quotable through legitimate access (search results or the post page). Never invent posts.
research_updates._doc: Fetched daily by GitHub Actions into candidates/updates/<date>.json, in parallel: lab, researcher and newsletter feeds (the Alan Turing Institute's generated feeds cover labs without RSS), Google News bridges for labs without feeds and for X and LinkedIn posts, Reddit, Bluesky and Hacker News. Duplicates are removed by canonical URL and headline. Dead links (404, 410) are logged in state/feed_health.json and skipped.

bluesky._doc: Bluesky public search (api.bsky.app, no login; only the first 100 results per query). Posts below min_likes are dropped.

world._doc: World Radar. Publisher feeds and Google News are fetched by GitHub Actions into candidates/news/<date>.json (headline, link, date, summary). Each headline is categorized in code (categories) and duplicates are merged. The run picks from them. A failing feed is listed in failed_sources and retried by the 06:50 run. A feed's section is only how candidates are grouped; each chosen item gets its own news category (prompts/world.md). lookback_hours on a feed overrides the default.

categories._doc: News categories (the same as prompts/world.md and the daily News page). Each headline gets the category whose keywords it matches most (whole words, title counts double), ties broken by the order here. With no match it takes its feed's default. Explainer feeds always stay explainers. Edit keywords freely. The 'other' bucket (sport, celebrity, local notices, crime blotter) is listed last and is usually skipped. weights multiply a category's score (leadership words count double, so 'prime minister resigns' is a leadership change, not general geopolitics).

google_news._doc: Google News RSS for every edition in 'editions' (India and US): topic sections, fixed searches (the first edition only, unless all_editions is true) and searches built from your interests. Links point to news.google.com and redirect to the publisher.

interest_query._doc: Searches built from config/interests.json, run for every edition: short phrases joined with OR, a few per query. Single lowercase words are skipped as too noisy.

world._doc_depth: Feeds with depth:true (The Conversation, Nature News, Quanta) explain why things happen; the World Radar pairs big stories with them.

youtube._doc: Shorts: queries are grouped by language and rotated, queries_per_day of them each day (100 quota units each, 10,000 a day). long_form: lectures, documentaries and talks for Daily Discovery, also rotated.

queries: basic Japanese phrases for beginners short

youtube._doc_languages: Only languages you understand. For languages you are learning, use beginner lessons taught in English or Hindi (purpose language_learning). Native videos in a learning language come only after config/languages.json sets native_content_ok to true for it.

channels._doc: Curated channels read through their free RSS feeds (no search quota). Handles are resolved to channel ids once with channels.list (1 unit) and cached in state/youtube_channels.json; stats come from videos.list (1 unit per 50 videos).

paper_tags._doc: The only tags a paper can get, in the arXiv radar and the weekly reading list. Fixed on purpose: reuse these, never invent new ones. Order matters: the first tag is shown first.

huggingface._doc: Hugging Face Daily Papers (successor to Papers with Code). Used as a quality signal (community upvotes) and an extra source of arXiv papers.

trending._doc: Trending models, datasets and spaces (sort=trendingScore) into candidates/hf/<date>.json, for research updates.

alphaxiv._doc: alphaXiv (undocumented API, read defensively). feeds: community lists over the last 7 days (Hot, Likes, Comments, GitHub). The API rejects the 'Twitter (X)' list (HTTP 400, Nov 2026), so X discussion comes through Hacker News, newsletters and web search. search: one search per interest in arxiv.coverage (the topic's 'search' text or its interest name); results land in candidates/arxiv/<date>.json -> interest_search and flag matching candidates with alphaxiv_interests.

notable_researchers._doc: Papers with one of these authors are flagged (notable_authors) in candidates so they are never missed. Keep a paper only if it also touches your interests. Edit freely.

podcasts._doc: Fetched daily by GitHub Actions into candidates/podcasts/<date>.json. Shows are looked up by name with the iTunes Search API (no feed URLs to maintain); each episode keeps its audio file so it plays on the page. episode_searches find single episodes on your interests. Edit freely. feeds are podcast RSS feeds read directly (no iTunes lookup).

paper_social._doc: Papers people are discussing: arXiv ids found in Reddit and Bluesky posts are added to the paper candidates (fetched from the arXiv API if new) with reddit_mentions, bluesky_mentions and bluesky_likes.
